claims.claim: Holding 50,000 connections open isn't the hard part. A properly tuned server in almost any modern stack can do that.
claims.why: The most connections any test used was 256, and none of them held long-lived WebSocket connections, so nothing shows whether 50,000 open connections can be held.

claims.claim: One Reverb process handles many thousands of connections without a worker per connection.
claims.why: Reverb was not benchmarked, and no test held thousands of connections.

claims.claim: Elixir/Phoenix is technically the best fit for this kind of product, but at 50k connections you don't need it.
claims.measured: elixir-phoenix I/O wait at 256 connections: 18,711 req/s, p99 19.16 ms, 160 MB
claims.why: Neither Phoenix nor Reverb was measured holding persistent connections at large scale, so the claim that Phoenix fits best and Reverb is enough at 50k cannot be checked.

claims.claim: Node.js or Go for the whole product: you'd give up speed in Laravel and gain nothing.
claims.measured: php-laravel 681 req/s plaintext and 149 req/s single DB query, vs go-gin 53,941 and 22,138, node-fastify 40,730 and 9,423
claims.why: For the normal-request part of the product, Go and Node measured roughly 25–150× the throughput of Laravel, so saying they 'gain nothing' points the wrong way on performance.

claims.claim: Soketi is Pusher-compatible and very efficient.
Centrifugo (Go) is very fast and proven at scale.
Standard PHP ties up one worker for every open connection, so it can't hold thousands at once (SSE or long-polling from Laravel).
claims.measured: php-laravel I/O wait (10 ms per request, 256 connections): 591 req/s, p50 412.91 ms, p99 458.02 ms
claims.why: With only 256 connections each waiting 10 ms, Laravel's median latency rose to about 413 ms, so only a handful of requests were being served at once; thousands of held connections are out of reach.

claims.claim: Out of the box, Reverb's PHP event loop can't go past about 1,024 connections without ext-uv.
claims.why: Reverb was not measured, and no test went above 256 connections.

claims.claim: In a reconnect storm, tens of thousands of widgets hitting the Laravel channel-auth endpoint within seconds can overwhelm PHP.
claims.measured: php-laravel 681–705 req/s (plaintext/JSON) and 149 req/s with one DB query, per core
claims.why: At about 150–700 req/s per core, tens of thousands of auth requests within a few seconds would need dozens of cores, so overwhelming PHP is consistent with the measurements.

claims.claim: Managed Pusher/Ably gets expensive at 10k–50k connections while the same load fits on a few VMs.
claims.why: Neither the connection capacity of Reverb nor that of any server at 10k–50k connections was measured.

claims.claim: For the first year (2,000 widgets), one modest VM can run everything, and the load test should hold up at these numbers.
claims.why: Reverb's connection capacity was not measured, and the request rate per widget is unknown, so whether one VM is enough cannot be checked.
